differentiationStatement: Vinyl-specific mop archetype explainer. Routes Surface Protector readers (LVP/LVT/sheet vinyl owners) to the right mop type, with a 4-archetype QuickPicks block. Does NOT compete with /best-mop (broad commercial roundup) or /how-to-clean-vinyl-floors (technique guide). Cuts steam mop and wet-string archetypes from the recommendation pool because manufacturer (Shaw) factory care explicitly forbids steam and high-water-volume application on plank vinyl.

categories.label: Flat-microfiber spray mop with refillable reservoir
categories.definingTraits: Refillable reservoir holds pH-neutral cleaner; fine-mist spray puts the lowest water volume on the floor of any wet-mop archetype. Machine-washable microfiber pad. Manufacturer-aligned with Shaw spray-and-dry-mop technique.

categories.label: Microfiber twist-bucket spin mop
categories.definingTraits: Wring-tightness control via foot-pedal centrifuge; thoroughly wrung microfiber head puts less water on the floor than a saturated sponge or string mop. Right archetype for sheet vinyl in larger rooms or when reservoir spray runs out too fast.

categories.label: Battery-powered scrubbing spray mop
examples: Bissell SpinWave Powered Hard Floor Mop
categories.definingTraits: Soft-touch motorized pads add scrubbing torque without escalating water volume. Adjustable water control via product-specific spray triggers. 4-5x price multiplier vs flat microfiber. Manufacturer-marketed sealed-hardwood/laminate/vinyl-safe.

categories.label: Disposable-pad spray mop (caveats apply)
categories.definingTraits: Cartridge-spray water volume is low; convenient (no laundering pads). Caveat: stock cartridge solutions are not pH-neutral across all formula variants — reload with a pH-neutral solution to align with Shaw factory care guidance.

definitionalSources.claim: Microfiber + spray (reservoir cartridge) is the manufacturer-recommended archetype for daily and weekly vinyl maintenance.

Independent 8-mop test of vinyl-floor mops ranked Rubbermaid Reveal Microfiber Spray Mop best-overall and explicitly warned against steam mops on vinyl: 'high heat and moisture can cause damage if seams or adhesives are breached'.
Wet string mops are forbidden on plank vinyl because seam-water wicks into adhesive and curls plank edges.
Family Handyman documents the seam-water mechanism on vinyl: 'too much water will infiltrate your vinyl floor's seams where it can affect the tile stickiness'.
Mainstream lifestyle roundups (BHG, Real Simple, The Spruce) name flat microfiber spray + microfiber twist as vinyl-safe archetypes; SpinWave and Tineco appear in motorized-scrubber slots.
definitionalSources.evidence: Cross-source triangulation against bhg.com / realsimple.com / thespruce.com archetype lists — see candidate-pool rows 7-9 in research doc.

decisions.reason: Support-guide explainer; no product roundup; readers ready to buy a specific SKU are routed to /best-mop (cluster flagship) where Amazon ASINs already live.
Page rank/score products is not the page's job; defining 4 archetypes and routing readers is. categoryEvidence with 4 categories replaces finalProducts for support-guide pageType.

Substantive claims are triangulated across Shaw factory care (primary), Bob Vila eight-mop lab round (tier-1 methodology), Family Handyman (tier-2 editorial), and BHG/Real Simple/The Spruce (tier-2 editorial). 5 named expert sources. ownerReviewsAnalyzed:0 — TCR does not run an LVP-flooring lab; no first-person testing claims are made.

decisions.decision: Steam mop archetype explicitly cut from QuickPicks.
decisions.reason: Shaw factory care forbids steam on resilient vinyl; Bob Vila category roundup explicitly warns against it. Including steam in any 'best mop for vinyl' list violates AGENTS rule #11 (zero fabrication of customer-first recommendations) — the page's job is to keep readers' floors under warranty.
